args.message:
fix: use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money

Per FIN-212, round_money must round half to even. The implementation
used ROUND_HALF_UP, which caused the nightly build to fail on
tests/test_money.py. Switch to ROUND_HALF_EVEN to match the spec and
the test expectations.

args.head: fix/bankers-rounding
args.title: fix: use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money
args.body:
## Summary

The nightly build fails because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` implemented `ROUND_HALF_UP`.

This change switches `round_money` to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, matching the FIN-212 spec and the test expectations:

- `round_money(Decimal("2.675")) == Decimal("2.68")`
- `round_money(Decimal("2.665")) == Decimal("2.66")` (banker's rounding)

## Testing

CI passed on branch `fix/bankers-rounding` (run `ci-0001`).

Requesting review from @alex.

## Summary

**Problem:** The nightly build of payments-service failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` was using `ROUND_HALF_UP`.

**Fix:**
- Created branch `fix/bankers-rounding` from `main`.
- Updated `src/money.py` to import and use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP`, so `round_money` now correctly implements banker's rounding per FIN-212 (e.g., `2.675 → 2.68`, `2.665 → 2.66`).
